title: The common section model represents the specified support comparisons
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $T$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion and $j:V=T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-size-convention], with comparison $
u_T^*\dashv
u_{T,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $F$ be an etale $A$-module sheaf, $F_p=
u_T^*F$, and $h:F_p	o J^ ullet$ a bounded-below injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $I^ ullet=
u_{T,*}J^ ullet$ and $a=
u_{T,*}(h)\circ\eta_F^0$. Assume that $a$ is an injective resolution representing the derived comparison unit, and use the canonical injective computations of derived sections and support kernels [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective, def-pur-support-cohomology].

With the inverse images $j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1},j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], let $ eta_F:
u_V^*(j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}F_p$ be the canonical comparison pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Under the sectionwise direct-image identification $j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}
u_{T,*}=
u_{V,*}j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}$, the ordinary units satisfy
$$j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(\eta_F^0)=
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\circ\eta_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F}^0.$$

For $W=T,V$, let $u_W:I^ ullet(W)	o J^ ullet(W)$ be the identity induced by direct-image evaluation, and let $u_C$ be its induced identity on $\ker(I^ ullet(T)	o I^ ullet(V))$. In the bounded-below derived category of $A$-modules, $Qu_T$ represents the unit-induced global comparison $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)	o R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F_p)$, and $Qu_V$, with coefficients identified by $ eta_F$, represents the corresponding global comparison on $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. The map $Qu_C$ represents the canonical supported comparison $c^C_{T,F}$ of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]. Explicitly, this specified comparison is $c^C_{T,F}=b_{C,F_p}\circ R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},\eta_F)$, where $\eta_F:F	o R
u_{T,*}F_p$ is the derived unit and $b_{C,F_p}$ is the kernel-normalized direct-image comparison of [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image]. These identifications use the given augmentations $a,h$, preserve the kernel inclusions and restriction arrows, and commute with chain maps between such augmented resolutions lifting morphisms of $F$. There is no assertion about connecting morphisms in this statement.

proof.text:
For each etale object $W	o T$, the definition of direct image gives $(
u_{T,*}J^n)(W)=J^n(W)$, and it gives the same map for every arrow of such objects. Thus the maps $u_T,u_V$ are identities of complexes, not just degreewise bijections: the differentials and the arrow $T\leftarrow V$ are the same on both sides. The support functor is the kernel of this arrow, with the induced action on morphisms. Hence its termwise application gives the stated $u_C$, with the same kernel inclusion. Likewise, on any etale $W	o V$, both $j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}
u_{T,*}J^n$ and $
u_{V,*}j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}J^n$ evaluate to $J^n(W	o T)$; this is the sectionwise restriction/direct-image identification in the question.

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit] with the given finite ring $A$, scheme $T$, open $j$ and sheaf $F$. In its notation $a_F=\beta_F^{-1}$ and $c_{F_p}$ is precisely the sectionwise identity of step 1. Its unit equation is
$$\nu_{V,*}(\beta_F^{-1})\circ j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(\eta_F^0)=\eta_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F}^0.$$
Postcompose by $\nu_{V,*}(\beta_F)$. Since a functor preserves inverse isomorphisms, this gives exactly
$$j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(\eta_F^0)=\nu_{V,*}(\beta_F)\circ\eta_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F}^0.$$
In particular the comparison here is the specified canonical pullback comparison, with its specified unit, rather than a new choice of isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $e:QI^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{T,*}F_p$ for the injective-computation isomorphism specified in the hypotheses. Those hypotheses say $e\circ Qa=\eta_F$. The canonical injective computation of a right derived functor is natural in chain maps by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Consequently, when the source $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)$ is identified with $QI^\bullet(T)$ by the augmentation $a$, the morphism $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},\eta_F)$ has identity matrix on $I^\bullet(T)$, with its target identified using $e$. To identify the next factor, $J^\bullet$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. The full-support case $C=T$ of [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image] says that the final-object comparison is represented by the sectionwise identity $I^\bullet(T)=J^\bullet(T)$. The global comparison is the composite of these two factors by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Its representative is therefore exactly $u_T$, with the source and target identifications coming from $a$ and $h$.

proof.text:
Put $F_V=j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F$, $J_V^ ullet=j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}J^ ullet$, and $h_V=(j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}h)\circ eta_F:
u_V^*F_V	o J_V^ ullet$. Restriction is exact and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], so $h_V$ is a bounded-below injective resolution. Apply [lem-pur-support-comparison-common-injectives] on the scheme $V$ to this resolution. It gives the injective etale resolution $a_V=
u_{V,*}(h_V)\circ\eta_{F_V}^0$, representing the derived unit on $V$. The sectionwise identity of step 1 identifies its target $
u_{V,*}J_V^ ullet$ with $j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}I^ ullet$. Step 2 then gives the actual equality of augmentations
$$a_V=
u_{V,*}(j_{\mathrm{pro}}^{-1}h)\circ
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\circ\eta_{F_V}^0=j_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(a).$$
Now repeat the two-factor calculation of step 3 on $V$, using $a_V,h_V$ and the global comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Its chain representative is the identity $I^ ullet(V)=J^ ullet(V)$, namely $u_V$. The source augmentation is the restriction of the given $a$, and $h_V$ uses exactly the required coefficient identification $ eta_F$.

proof.text: Apply the same calculation to the additive kernel functor $\Gamma_C$ defined in [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Under the injective-computation isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the equality $e\circ Qa=\eta_F$ from step 3 means that $R\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},\eta_F)$ is represented by the identity of $\ker(I^\bullet(T)\to I^\bullet(V))$, with its source identified by the given augmentation $a$. The second factor $b_{C,F_p}$ of the explicitly specified $c^C_{T,F}$ is, by the normalization in [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image], the identity between that kernel and $\ker(J^\bullet(T)\to J^\bullet(V))$. Its hypothesis of a K-injective representative holds by the bounded-below injective result used in step 3. Thus the composite has representative $u_C$. This uses the normalization of $b$ and the displayed definition of $c^C_{T,F}$ in the statement; compatibility with the two other terms alone would not determine a supported map.

proof.text:
Let $f:F	o F'$ and $t:J^ ullet	o J'^ ullet$ be a chain map between two such augmented resolutions lifting $
u_T^*f$, so $t\circ h=h'\circ
u_T^*f$. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction unit gives
$$
u_{T,*}(t)\circ a=
u_{T,*}(t\circ h)\circ\eta_F^0=
u_{T,*}(h')\circ\eta_{F'}^0\circ f=a'\circ f.$$
On $W=T,V$ the maps $
u_{T,*}(t)(W)$ and $t(W)$ are literally equal by the direct-image formula. They commute with the restriction arrows because $t$ is a morphism of sheaf complexes. If $s\in J^n(T)$ restricts to zero on $V$, then $\mathrm{res}(t(s))=t(\mathrm{res}(s))=0$; the same equality proves that the induced kernel map commutes with the kernel inclusion. These equalities commute with all three identity representatives. Localization preserves these equalities, and the canonical derived comparisons used above are natural. This proves the claimed naturality and preservation of the two arrows on the specified augmentations.
